why_angle: Every cited Soundcore page gives the AeroClip 2's 8 h/32 h and the C50i's 7 h/28 h with no codec or volume conditions, and none says the C50i also plays LDAC. Soundcore's own support tables show that with LDAC on, the AeroClip 2 falls to 5 h at 50% volume (3 h at 100%) and the C50i drops multipoint. This page is the only one with that fully maker-sourced battery and codec fact, which removes LDAC and battery as reasons to pay for the AeroClip 2 and leaves the call microphones as the reason.

page.answer: Short answer. Soundcore AeroClip 2 vs C50i: buy the C50i unless calls come first. Both support LDAC, and with LDAC on, the AeroClip 2 battery falls from 8 to 5 hours at 50% volume, under the C50i's rated 7 hours. Its microphone setup (4 mics plus 2 voice pickup units) is the edge you pay for.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Price: Soundcore's US store has the AeroClip 2 at $169.99 and the C50i at $39.98. That is a $130.01 gap (169.99 − 39.98), and the AeroClip 2 costs 4.25× as much (169.99 ÷ 39.98). The C50i's list price is $69.99.
  • Music battery on LDAC: the AeroClip 2 loses 3 h, 37.5% of its rating (8 − 5 = 3; 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375). That leaves it 2 h behind the C50i's rated 7 h (7 − 5 = 2). Soundcore rates the C50i's 7 h at 50% volume in Bass Boost mode and names no codec for it.
  • Call time: the AeroClip 2 lasts 0.5 h longer per charge, about 11% (5 − 4.5 = 0.5; 0.5 ÷ 4.5 = 0.11). With the case it lasts 2 h longer (20 − 18).
  • Fast charge: on the AeroClip 2, 10 min gives 4 h, which is 2.5 min of charging per hour of play (10 ÷ 4). On the C50i, 10 min gives 2 h, or 5 min per hour (10 ÷ 2).
  • Case: both cases hold three full recharges. For the AeroClip 2, (32 − 8) ÷ 8 = 3; for the C50i, (28 − 7) ÷ 7 = 3.
  • A lost earbud: one replacement AeroClip 2 ear grip costs $79.99 at Soundcore's store, 47% of a new set (79.99 ÷ 169.99). A whole new C50i set costs $39.98, which is $40.01 less (79.99 − 39.98).

LDAC on both, and what it costs you

LDAC sends more audio data over Bluetooth than AAC, and the radio uses more power to do it. Soundcore's own battery table for the AeroClip 2 shows the cost. On AAC at 50% volume with soundcore Signature mode, it plays for 8 h. Turn LDAC on and it plays for 5 h at 50% volume, or 3 h at 100% (4.5 h on AAC at 100%). The same table puts call mode at 5 h at 50% volume. Soundcore adds that custom EQ and dual-device connection also raise the power draw.

The C50i lists the same codecs: SBC, AAC and LDAC. Its trade-off is a different one. Soundcore's C50i FAQ says: "Dual connection is not supported when using LDAC. Please disable LDAC and enable the dual connection function." So on the C50i you choose between LDAC and staying connected to a phone and a laptop at once. Soundcore's AeroClip 2 support pages do say dual-device connection can't be switched on during a call or online meeting.

LDAC only matters on Android. Kopfbox (Markus) says the AeroClip 2's LDAC is for Android users only and isn't available while 3D Spatial Audio is on. Expert Reviews' Andy White heard LDAC from a Google Pixel 11 and AAC from an iPhone 13 Pro. White found the LDAC gain smaller on open-ear buds than on sealed ones. On an iPhone, both earbuds play AAC. So the case for the AeroClip 2 comes down to its call hardware and its faster charge, not its codec or its battery. If calls are what you buy for, {buy:soundcore-aeroclip-2}. For music, runs and everyday listening, {buy:soundcore-c50i}.

Not recommended

The soundcore C40i costs $49.99 at Soundcore's store today, $10.01 more than the C50i. Soundcore's FAQ lists it with Bluetooth 5.4, SBC and AAC only (no LDAC) and IPX4 water resistance. The C50i has Bluetooth 6.0, LDAC and IP55. HeadphoneCheck's Sven Opitz got at least 7 h per charge and 21 h with the case, against the C50i's rated 28 h with its case.
